clue.text: Kit he's dropped, the fool

indicators.note: dropped tells us those letters are let fall from the longer word

parts.note: kit is clothing, gear one wears
the word he's gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone has let their kit fall and is branded an idiot for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person, a synonym of fool.

clue.text: King taken round the principal town of Surrey

indicators.note: taken round means the king's letters go around the next word

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's king
taken as written
a head is a principal, as of a school

explanation.surface: A monarch is shown round Surrey's main town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like an adjective on 'town' but gives HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Leatherhead is a town in the English county of Surrey, south-west of London.

clue.text: Out of tune, diva later suffered

indicators.note: out of tune suggests notes in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An opera singer, singing off-key, paid for it afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To travail is to toil painfully, so travailed means suffered or laboured.

clue.text: Newspaper has written about extremely remote holiday properties

parts.note: The Times is the newspaper this very puzzle appears in

indicators.note: written about means the word has is set down around something else

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a feature on far-flung holiday homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Timeshares are holiday homes owned jointly, each owner using them for a set period yearly.

clue.text: Parasite's gone for reprimand

parts.note: a tick is a blood-sucking parasite
off means gone or departed

explanation.surface: The parasite has gone, so someone gets told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick off is informal for to scold or reprimand.

clue.text: Suggest assembling in Missouri for classic film

definitions.meaning: an invitation to gather in the main city of the state of Missouri

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally proposes a meeting in a Missouri city and is also the title of a 1944 musical film.

clue.text: Foreign writer is turning people on

indicators.note: turning says the word is is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
men are people
taken as written

explanation.surface: An overseas author is said to excite the public.
explanation.walkthrough: Georges Simenon was the Belgian author of the Maigret novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was a Belgian novelist writing in French, hence foreign to the British solver.

clue.text: Become debilitated, inhaling a second joint

indicators.note: inhaling means taking the other letters inside

parts.note: to rot is to decay or deteriorate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grows weak after a second puff on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette but means a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven.

clue.text: Guy consumes a spicy sort of meat

indicators.note: consumes means the first word swallows the letter

parts.note: a guy is a rope steadying a tent or mast, as is a stay
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man eats some spiced meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' reads as a man but is a supporting rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a South-East Asian dish of spiced meat grilled on skewers with peanut sauce.

clue.text: Laugh wildly, catching a youngster dressing

indicators.note: catching means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: to scream with laughter is to laugh wildly
taken as written
a lad is a boy, a youngster

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks with laughter as they grab hold of a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a British bottled condiment, a type of salad dressing.

clue.text: Changed position during talk, showing discretion

indicators.note: during talk says the word is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sailing boat that has tacked has changed course or position

explanation.surface: Someone shifts their stance in a conversation to seem discreet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is sensitivity in dealing with others, close in meaning to discretion.

clue.text: Shoddy collection of articles stored by firm

indicators.note: stored by means put inside the firm's letters

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a heap is a pile, a collection of things

explanation.surface: A company keeps a pile of poor-quality goods in its warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is informal for cheap and of poor quality, i.e. shoddy.

clue.text: Government department requiring test on cars

indicators.note: in an across answer, on places the test word after the cars

parts.note: Minis are small British cars
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: A ministry insists vehicles undergo a roadworthiness check.
explanation.definitionFit: A ministry is a department of government headed by a minister.

clue.text: Doctor overrates it as health-promoting medicine

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician exaggerates the benefits of a tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative is a tonic or medicine that restores health and strength.

clue.text: With regular absences, four fail examination

indicators.note: regular absences means every other letter is missing, so alternate letters are kept

explanation.surface: Students who skip class often find that four of them fail the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

clue.text: Last working day's interminable, lacking possibilities for socialising?

parts.note: Friday, abbreviated FRI, ends the working week
interminable means never-ending, without end

explanation.surface: Friday drags on endlessly with no chance of a social life.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no companions leaves one with nobody to socialise with, the question mark marking the playful definition.

clue.text: Help stop a horse entering estate

indicators.note: entering means the pieces go inside the estate word

parts.note: land is an estate, property
an end is a stop
taken as written
H is slang for heroin, called horse

explanation.surface: Someone helps halt a horse coming onto the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend a hand means to help someone.

clue.text: Marinade, for example, is on offer at commercial centre

indicators.note: on places the word is after the offer word

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer, as in a bid for a contract
taken as written

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle pair of letters of the word commercial

explanation.surface: A marinade is being promoted for sale in a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade softens meat, so it is one example of a meat softener.

clue.text: Have short illness after run? Train under their supervision

indicators.note: after puts the illness word behind the run letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an ailment is an illness

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill after a jog and is put in charge of training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb, but it is a railway train run by railwaymen.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway workers oversee the running of trains, so a train is under their supervision.

clue.text: Wine selected from clarets in Agen

indicators.note: selected from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wine is chosen from Bordeaux reds in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: No approval for retreat

parts.note: taken as written
OK is a sign of approval

explanation.surface: A request for a getaway is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a secluded corner, a quiet retreat.

clue.text: I held leg, injured in battle

indicators.note: injured suggests damage, so the letters are bent out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier clutches a wounded leg during combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgehill (1642) was the first major battle of the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgehill names the 1642 battle in Warwickshire between Royalists and Parliamentarians.

clue.text: Currency you increased in value with speech

indicators.note: with speech says the words are heard spoken aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: you rose means you went up in value

explanation.surface: Your currency rose in value after a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency of most EU states, so euros is money in that currency.

clue.text: Dope about to make progress

indicators.note: about means the information word goes around the other

parts.note: dope and gen are both slang for information
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drugs help someone get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on means to advance or make progress.

clue.text: To secure sovereignty, beat emperor

indicators.note: to secure here means to hold something inside, so the beating word encloses the other

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them
the Raj was British sovereign rule in India

explanation.surface: A ruler must fight to win and keep power.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor, reigning from AD 98 to 117.

clue.text: Speed of old car not constant

indicators.note: not means the constant's letter is left out

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, rickety car
C is the symbol for a constant, as in the speed of light

explanation.surface: An old banger can't keep up a steady speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rate means speed, as in travelling at a fast rate.

clue.text: Upper-class girl gripped by crazy desire in part of Africa

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: a mania is a wild craving
U is the label for upper-class usage
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A posh young woman is seized with a passion for travelling in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauritania is a country in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Revolutionary racket is brought in by Father Christmas

indicators.note: brought in by means carried inside the Father Christmas word

parts.note: Father Christmas is Santa Claus
a racket is a din, a loud noise
taken as written

explanation.surface: Santa arrives bringing a noisy present.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandinistas were members of Nicaragua's revolutionary socialist movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sandinista is a member of the Nicaraguan revolutionary front, so a kind of revolutionary.

clue.text: Weight-loss plan takes long time

parts.note: to be dying for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Slimming programmes take ages to show results.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a regime of eating designed to reduce weight.
